title: Lift & Latch — Platform sync notes (control plane / routing / auth / quotas)
content:
Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Lena, Devon, Priya (remote), plus ad-hoc: Sam (SRE) and Noor (QA)

Purpose: quick weekly sync focused on "lift" items (things to raise across teams) and "latch" items (things we must pin down before next deploy). This is a lightweight capture — action owners + due dates noted.

Top-level status summary (by area):
- Control plane: slow steady progress on rollout of v2 lease allocator; still seeing 6% repro of lease starvation in staging. Canary window extended to 48h.
- Routing: routing-fallback changes merged to canary; initial latency improvement ~3–5ms p50 for small-text flows, but a 0.8% increase in 99th when bursty traffic hits legacy pool.
- Auth: short outage on 2028-05-14 (15m) traced to token key rotation bug — root cause fix + hotpatch in prod; follow-up: add key-rotation feature flag.
- Quotas: quota engine prototype supports rolling window tokens but needs eviction tuning (current mem high-water mark 72%).

Notes / discussion:
1) Control plane — lease allocator (Marco)
   - Observed: lease starvation traces cluster around 10–12k concurrent prefixes with high prefix churn.
   - Hypothesis: allocator fairness heuristic over-prioritizes new prefixes, starving long-lived leases under heavy churn.
   - Mitigation being tested: add exponential backoff for re-acquire attempts + sticky weighting (branch: allocator/sticky-backoff).
   - Action: Marco to run a 24h stress on staging with churn generator (JIRA: PLTFRM-3421). Expected results due 2028-05-19.
   - Blocker: staging is low on quota GPUs this week; SRE (Sam) to approve temporary burst capacity by EOD 5/17.

2) Routing — fallback policy and pool migration (Lena)
   - Canary metrics: p50 down slightly, p99 up in burst scenario. Investigating how fallback path re-writes affect TCP connection reuse.
   - Idea: maintain connection pool affinity for 60s even after fallback to avoid new TLS handshakes. Quick perf experiment planned (PR #1819).
   - UX concern: some tenant routes observed more frequent model downgrades than expected (conversation with solutions-eng).
   - Action: Lena to add logging tags for tenant-tier and route-policy to help correlate. Follow-up in next sync.

3) Auth — token key rotation outage (Devon)
   - Incident summary: key-rotation job attempted to rotate primary key while HSM transiently rejected KMS load; rotation completed but some in-flight tokens failed validation for ~15m.
   - Short-term: revert to previous rotation schedule and roll out hotpatch to gate rotation when KMS lat > 150ms. Patch rolled 5/15 02:12 UTC.
   - Long-term: implement retry + exponential jitter logic and add feature flag to disable auto-rotation per environment.
   - Action: Devon to open follow-up ticket with migration runbook and feature-flag gating: expected 5/24.

4) Quotas — rolling-window engine and eviction (Priya)
   - Observed mem pressure: high-cardinality tenant keys for embedding-heavy workloads push mem to 72% on smallest quota nodes. Eviction policy FIFO leads to poor hit-rate.
   - Proposal: switch to LRU with TTL tiers and a small hot-set cache for heavy tenants. Prototype exists in branch quotas/lru-ttl.
   - Risk: LRU introduces CPU overhead; need perf baseline.
   - Action: Priya to benchmark LRU vs FIFO on a 10k-tenant replay by 5/22 and report CPU/RAM/tradeoffs.

Cross-cutting items:
- Observability gaps: need token-level traces for routing fallthroughs and quota rejections. Decided to add a lightweight trace header and sample at 1% initially. (Owner: Marco + Lena, due 5/24)
- Rollout policy: for the next week, we agreed to restrict major allocator/routing changes to off-peak windows (sat 02:00-06:00 UTC) until the sticky-backoff proven in staging.
- Canary telemetry: add a 'canary-cohort' label to metrics for easier filtering in dashboards. (Owner: Aisha, dashboard PR 5/19)

Open questions / brainstorm snippets (raw):
- Could quotas use a multi-level cache (edge + regional + controlplane) to reduce central mem needs? rough thought: edge caches of tenant tokens with short TTLs.
- What if we used predictive allocation: track 1h moving-average prefix growth to pre-warm leases for tenants that show growth spikes?
- Quick sketch: maintain per-tenant burst budget that is drained into short-lived burst leases (tunable). May help priority fairness.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Marco: run allocator churn test in staging, collect traces (due 2028-05-19).
- Sam (SRE): approve temporary staging GPU burst for test (due 2028-05-17 EOD).
- Lena: add tenant-tier logging to routing fallbacks; create dashboard query (due 2028-05-20).
- Devon: write rotation runbook + feature-flag ticket (due 2028-05-24).
- Priya: LRU prototype perf benchmark vs FIFO; publish results (due 2028-05-22).
- Aisha: add canary-cohort label and PR for dashboards (due 2028-05-19).
- Marco+Lena: implement trace header sampling at 1% and add to canary pipelines (due 2028-05-24).

Risks & escalations:
- If allocator starvation persists after sticky-backoff, consider temporary throttle on prefix-creation from hosters — this requires coordination with solutions and support.
- Memory pressure in quota nodes might require a short-term scale-up; finance approval needed for extra nodes (Priya to open finance request).

Meeting artifacts and references:
- Allocator experiment branch: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/allocator/sticky-backoff (PR pending)
- Routing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1819
- Incident timeline (auth rotation): Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLTFM/Auth+Rotation+Incident+2028-05-14
- Linear: PLTFRM-3421 (allocator churn), PLTFRM-3480 (quota eviction tuning)

Next sync: short follow-up on 2028-05-24 to review allocator experiment results and quota perf numbers (15 minutes). If major regressions, we'll convene an emergency deep-dive.

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Remind solutions-eng to prepare a small tenant sample for routing affinity tests (names: Acorn, Bluefin).
- Add a one-liner in incident postmortem about key rotation coupling to KMS latency.
- Check whether TLS session cache size on proxies needs bumping when we do connection affinity change.

End of notes.

Raw edit history: quick doc created by Aisha during post-standup and shared to #platform-controlplane; save to Drive for tracking.
